A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QPE-based causal-discovery work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original bivariate causal-discovery and multivariate causal-ordering experiments, including benchmark results, hyperparameter studies, convergence analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original results.

M1.justification: The stated QPE-f neural basis-test loss changes from a residual norm in v1 Section 3.4 to its expectation in v2 Section 4.3. This is a limited loss-formulation refinement; the PDFs do not establish changed implementation or retraining. QPE-k, flow fitting, and FICO's ordering steps remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same 24 bivariate benchmarks and multivariate evaluations remain, including confounded synthetic datasets, Sachs, and Syntren. The convergence and heteroscedastic-Gaussian scenarios already appeared in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain the same baseline methods, including the 21 bivariate baselines and multivariate ordering comparators. v2's focused FICO–CaPS runtime table redisplays an existing comparison; newly cited related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained evaluation descriptions preserve preprocessing, metrics, training configurations, and the convergence study's sample-size sweep. Some benchmark settings disappear from the documentation, but no replacement settings or changed evaluation procedure are reported.

E4.justification: Hyperparameter tuning, sample-size convergence, confounding robustness, heteroscedastic-Gaussian sensitivity, and runtime analyses are retained. v2 redistributes v1's multivariate supplementary analyses across Sections D.3–D.7 without adding a new analysis.

E5.justification: v1 Section 5.2 specifies 50 sub-tests for the synthetic benchmarks; v2 omits this count. Existing error bars, tabulated plus/minus reporting, and the sensitivity study's 100-sub-test averaging remain. This is reduced statistical reporting, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: A qualitative finding is narrowed: v1 Figure 2 describes QPE-f matching the true QPE trend along the Y-axis, whereas v2 Figure 3 restricts the match to high-density areas. Matched numerical results and plotted data are unchanged. In particular, v2 Table 3 copies the FICO and CaPS runtimes from v1 Table 10.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit Assumption 3.7 on competing-direction Wronskians and Corollary 3.8 with a short identifiability proof. This formalizes and sharpens v1's surrounding discussion. The k+2-dimensional non-identifiability result and Fisher-information derivations are retained; their relocation and renumbering are not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims remain finite-span QPE identifiability, two bivariate discovery methods, and Fisher-information-based causal ordering. The stronger emphasis on FICO's efficiency does not introduce a new headline contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains that the known-basis requirement prevents direct application to PNL models with unknown transformation g. It also discusses difficulty assessing Assumption 3.7 and specifies that FICO's assumptions have only a qualitative interpretation under the heteroscedastic-Gaussian setting. General concerns about FICO's interpretability and testability already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: v2 drops v1's general synthetic-benchmark specification of 1,000 samples per sub-test and ER4/SF4 graph density. Most implementation and hyperparameter details remain in Appendices C and D. These omissions reduce reproducibility information without establishing an actual change to experimental settings.

R1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Guo et al. (2023), Reizinger et al. (2023), and Jalaldoust et al. (2025), distinguishing their assumptions from the paper's observational setting. Conversely, the Sachs and Syntren source references are removed although those evaluations remain.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: general QPE theory and bivariate discovery become separate sections, appendix identifiability and Gaussian-QPE discussion move into the main text, and the main multivariate experiment section shifts to runtime efficiency. The supplementary multivariate material is reorganized into several dedicated subsections, alongside rewritten theoretical explanations.

P2.justification: v2 adds a theorem-dependency diagram and an Assumption 3.5 row in Table 1. It moves the real-world ODR table to the appendix and creates a main-text runtime summary from existing rows. The redundant main-text benchmark figure is removed while the full appendix plot remains; existing empirical graphics are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the identifiability conditions and unknown-PNL limitation clearer, and its dependency diagram improves navigation through the theory. However, it removes basic benchmark sample-size, replication-count, and graph-density information while retaining the same quantitative evidence. The gains in theoretical clarity and losses in reproducibility create a material tradeoff whose net effect on overall quality is not reliably clear.
